title: Register as a GNWT bidder
summary: Create a free bidder account on the GNWT Contract Event Opportunities website to see procurement events, get email updates and submit bids.
steps: Read the official bidder registration guide|Open the Contract Event Opportunities website and choose "Register as a Bidder"|Accept the Terms of Agreement and complete the registration form|Watch for a confirmation email; approval takes up to 2 business days|After approval, look for the approval notice and a separate email with your username and password
notes: Duplicate registrations for the same company are denied. Registration is free (supplier FAQ). Source does not name the unit behind GNWTBidders, so the guide is assigned to the department.

title: Fix a sign-in problem on the GNWT contracts website
summary: If you forgot your sign-in details or cannot reach the Contract Event Opportunities website, the SAM Help Desk handles systems issues.
steps: Try the official change or reset password guide|For sign-in or systems problems, contact the SAM Help Desk|For account approvals or supplier account updates, contact GNWT Bidders at GNWTBidders@gov.nt.ca
notes: Source also lists (867) 767-9129 as the Yellowknife local number for systems issues.

title: Learn how to bid on a GNWT procurement event
summary: Official guides explain how to move around the contracts website, bid on an event and manage your bids.
steps: Read the website navigation guide|Read the Bidding on an Event guide|Use the Manage Bids guide to track your submissions|Send questions about a specific event in writing to the person named in its procurement documents, within the timelines in the Instructions to Bidders
notes: The rule about written questions comes from the supplier FAQ.

title: Register under the Business Incentive Policy
summary: The Business Incentive Policy (BIP) gives registered NWT-owned and operated businesses a bid adjustment in GNWT procurement. Registration is handled by Industry, Tourism and Investment.
steps: Read the eligibility criteria on the official BIP page|Download the BIP application form|Gather the supporting documents the form asks for|Search the public BIP Registry to confirm a registration|For guidance, contact the BIP Monitoring Office or your regional Economic Development Officer
notes: Registry search: https://www.iti.gov.nt.ca/en/services/business-incentive-program-bip/search-bip-registry. Source phone numbers belong to named staff, so only the shared email is listed here. This app does not assess eligibility or certify businesses.

title: Attend GNWT procurement training
summary: Procurement Shared Services runs online webinars on contracting with the GNWT, using the Contract Event Opportunities website and completing Business Incentive Policy forms.
steps: Pick a session on the official training page and use its registration link|To book a separate session for your business or group, email Procurement Training|To ask about a French-language session, email Procurement Training
notes: Session dates change each season. Link to the page instead of copying dates; review monthly.

title: Ask a question about GNWT procurement
summary: Procurement Shared Services answers general questions about doing business with the GNWT and has offices in Fort Smith, Hay River, Inuvik and Yellowknife.
steps: Email or call Procurement Questions|Or contact the Procurement Shared Services office in your region|For a question about a specific open procurement, write to the person named in its procurement documents instead
notes: Regional office numbers stay on the official page; the guide links instead of copying them.

title: Raise a concern about a GNWT procurement
summary: The Vendor Complaint Process gives vendors a way to escalate concerns about GNWT procurement, from an enquiry escalation up to a formal complaint.
steps: Start with the Vendor Enquiry Escalation Form|If needed, continue with the Vendor Notice of Protest Form|Then the Vendor Formal Complaint Form|Read the Vendor Complaint Process document for details
notes: Source page does not say how to return completed forms or list timelines. A separate Vendor Request for Independent Review Form is also linked. Unit inferred from the shared PSS phone line; confirm.

title: Submit an invoice to the GNWT
summary: Email invoices to Financial and Employee Shared Services, the fastest route, or mail or drop them off at a regional centre. Include every required item to avoid delays.
steps: Check that your invoice includes every required item|Email it to financial_sharedservices@gov.nt.ca, or mail or drop it off at a regional Financial and Employee Shared Services centre|Expect processing within 20 days if BIP-registered, or 30 days otherwise, counted from when the GNWT receives the invoice
notes: This app never accepts or stores invoices. Phone is the Financial general inquiries line from the FESS page.

title: Ask about an invoice payment
summary: To check on a payment, email Financial and Employee Shared Services or call a regional service centre, and have your invoice number ready.
steps: Find your invoice number|Email financial_sharedservices@gov.nt.ca with the invoice number|Or call a regional Financial Shared Services centre; numbers are on the official Submitting Invoices page
notes: This app shows no payment status. Payments are processed within 20 or 30 days from receipt, not the invoice date.

title: Set up direct deposit for supplier payments
summary: Suppliers can be paid by direct deposit. Complete the official form and return the signed original to Financial and Employee Shared Services.
steps: Download the official Direct Deposit form|Complete and sign it; choose email notification to hear as soon as a payment is processed|Return the signed original by mail or in person to a regional Financial Shared Services centre
notes: This app never collects banking details. The supplier FAQ wording about returning the form differs slightly from the Direct Deposit page; the guide follows the Direct Deposit page.

title: Bid on City of Yellowknife contracts
summary: The City of Yellowknife runs its own bidding system, separate from the GNWT Contract Event Opportunities website.
steps: Create a free supplier account on the City bidding system to preview public bids|Registering for a specific bid has a one-time fee|Set notifications for the bid categories you want
notes: Municipal service, not GNWT. Shown so users do not mistake City registration for territorial bidder registration. Phone hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
